answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token as an anchor before it may submit bids, with voting weight capped per locked token rather than per account. Splitting funds across a tide of freshly created accounts then adds no influence; to dominate decisions, an attacker must acquire and immobilize a large share of the token supply, paying market cost and losing access to those funds while they are locked. A cipher can protect private bid details, but it does not replace this economic barrier.
